summary: The author urges the FCC to condition E-Rate funding on daily screen time limits to better protect children's educational outcomes and brain development. The author argues that limiting screen time in schools and libraries would improve student learning outcomes and reduce the costs associated with screen-based learning. They cite evidence showing that student math and reading scores have been declining since 2012, despite the push for digital learning. The author also cites a 2020 study from UCLA that found no improvement in educational outcomes with increased computer access. The comment emphasizes the need for E-Rate funding to be tied to educational outcomes, specifically by requiring more restrictions on screen use during instructional hours to help teachers teach effectively and protect students from distractions and harmful content. The comment supports the idea of implementing daily screen time limits to ensure that screens are used appropriately and not for recreational purposes during school hours. The text argues for requiring screen time limits for schools to improve educational outcomes and student well-being, citing empirical evidence that reducing screen use benefits learning and well-being.
